title: America's biggest power grid operator issues data center warning
key_facts: David Souder, executive director of system operations at PJM Interconnection, which coordinates electricity across all or parts of 13 states and the District of Columbia, said on Thursday 15 Oct 2026 that data-centre demand leaves the grid with 'little room for error' (Newsweek).

He said year-round demand from data centres, plus unusually warm or cold weather arriving earlier and staying later, is eroding the spring and autumn low-demand periods used to take generators and lines offline for maintenance.
Souder: new demand is mostly from data centres and other large loads, and their use does not fluctuate much with the weather; it is a 12-month, 24/7 phenomenon.
He said expanding demand is outpacing new transmission and supply, turning maintenance windows into potential periods of significant grid stress.
Earlier this week the Department of Energy issued an emergency order directing PJM to bring specified generating units online when needed to reduce blackout risk in the mid-Atlantic.

The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) blocked a PJM plan that would have let new data centres and other users of at least 50 megawatts connect without matching new generation if they accepted possible power cuts; FERC said key provisions appeared to intrude on state authority over retail electricity service.
Newsweek says data centres have become a political flashpoint ahead of the November midterm elections.
quote_evidence: America's largest power grid operator has warned that surging electricity demand from data centers is contributing to an environment that leaves the system with “little room for error.”

Meanwhile, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, or FERC, blocked a proposed PJM plan allowing new data centers and other large users requiring at least 50 megawatts to connect without matching new generating capacity if they agreed to possible power cuts during periods of grid stress.
The FERC rejected the framework, however, saying that key provisions appeared to intrude on state authority over retail electricity service.
why_it_matters_hint: The grid that serves 13 states says data-centre demand is shrinking the quiet periods it uses to repair and upgrade the system.
notes: Souder's remarks were made Thursday 15 Oct 2026, one day before the window. The DOE emergency order (12 Oct 2026) was in our 14 Oct 2026 edition; the FERC rejection was already in the 14 Oct 2026 pool. New today is the operator's own warning.
